When they had just reached the south, spies exploited tensions between the northern envoys and the Central State to relieve frontier pressure. Ba was killed, Qian was detained in Haozhou, and it was publicly declared that the envoy had been murdered by men from Bian.
The Chinese names only spies (諜) who sow discord and an impersonal public claim (聲言); it does not make Li Jing their master or name the court as speaker.
For an offense he was demoted to commander of cavalry and infantry at Xuzhou.
For an offense he was demoted to commander of cavalry and infantry at Xu Prefecture.
The posting is 許州, Xu Prefecture (Xuchang), not 徐州 Xuzhou.

Before long, citing prolonged illness, he requested release from military command and was granted the honorary title of Grand Preceptor and appointed military governor of the Zhongwu Army.
Before long, citing prolonged illness, he requested release from military command and was granted the honorary title of Acting Grand Commandant and appointed military governor of the Zhongwu Army.
檢校太尉 is the honorary acting Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor (太師/太傅).

The literal field likewise renders 檢校太尉 as Grand Preceptor; Acting Grand Commandant is the correct title.

Pacification Commissioner Lei Youzhong assigned Jixun five hundred troops to hold the two eastern gates. When the rebels attacked Mizhou Fort, Jixun led his men fighting in retreat all the way to Jiazhou, defeated them, and returned with a yellow parasol and gold-plated spears as trophies.

Pacification Commissioner Lei Youzhong assigned Jixun five hundred troops to hold the two eastern gates. When the rebels attacked Mimou Fort, Jixun led his men fighting in retreat all the way to Jiazhou, defeated them, and returned with a yellow parasol and gold-plated spears as trophies.
彌牟砦 is Mimou Fort, not Mizhou; the original confuses a distinct toponym.

The literal field repeats Mizhou for 彌牟砦; Mimou Fort matches the Chinese name.

He rose through successive appointments as vice commander of the Palace Guard for infantry and cavalry, deputy commander of the infantry, observation commissioner of Yongzhou, and deputy overall director of the Jingyuan route concurrently administering Weizhou.

歷步軍馬軍殿前都虞候 lists three successive vice-commander posts (infantry, cavalry, Palace Front), not one fused Palace Guard office.
He died at the age of seventy-eight. Court audiences were suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor.
He died at the age of seventy-eight. Court audiences were suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Commandant.
The posthumous grant is 太尉 (Grand Commandant), not 太師 Grand Preceptor.

Ba was appointed overall commander of the Xing-Ming route on the western flank before the imperial carriage and additionally served under Li Jilong as battle formation commissioner on the eastern flank, garrisoned at Chenzhou.

Fan Zhongyan declared him cunning, timid, and ignorant of military affairs. He was reassigned to the Jingyuan route as concurrently deputy pacification, frontier strategy, and pacification commissioner.

Fan Zhongyan declared him cunning, timid, and ignorant of military affairs. He was reassigned to the Jingyuan route as concurrently deputy expeditionary, frontier-strategy, and pacification commissioner.
The concurrent titles are 招討、經略、安撫副使; 招討 is an expeditionary commission, not a second pacification title.

Soon word came that the enemy had pulled up their palisades and crossed the frontier moat. Huaimin entered Baodingchuan Fort. The enemy destroyed the plank bridge, cut off his retreat, made twenty-four separate crossings to pass their army through, and surrounded him.

Soon word came that the enemy had pulled up their palisades and crossed the frontier moat. Huaimin entered Dingchuan Fort to hold it. The enemy destroyed the plank bridge, cut off his retreat, made twenty-four separate crossings to pass their army through, and surrounded him.
入保定川砦 is the verb phrase 入保 plus the fort 定川砦, not a toponym Baodingchuan.
